To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a large proportion of genes exhibit mRNA-proteomics discordance in a growth phase dependent manner, (2) this discordance is more prominent in genes encoding proteins that are functionally related, and (3) the discordance is not a random event, rather it is a result of a concerted action of mRNA and protein degradation mechanisms.
a substantial proportion of genes in S. coelicolar exhibit mRNA-protein dynamics that are divergent in nature and that these divergences are often observed for functionally related groups of genes.
the mRNA and protein expression patterns of many S. coelicolar genes diverge during growth and adaptation to stationary phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of novel genes and pathways that are involved in dynamic processes, and provides an example of how the analysis of divergent mRNA-protein dynamics can lead to the discovery of new biological knowledge.
the identification and analysis of divergent mRNA-protein dynamics and the implications of such findings on the understanding of cellular processes in S. coelicolo
the identification of novel genes with divergent mRNA-protein dynamics in S. coeliccolor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mRNA and proteins are not always concordant, and that such discordance may be more common than previously thought.
the overall dynamics in the transcriptome is consistent with the proteome but the detailed analysis reveals significant divergence at a gene level.
while the majority of the genes in S. coelicologer are regulated by a similar mechanism at the mRNA and protein levels, a significant number of genes exhibit divergent patterns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although mRNA and protein levels may be highly correlated, there are many cases where the dynamics of mRNA and proteins do not follow each other.
the dynamics of mRNA-protein relationships are more complex than previously thought and that the underlying mechanisms may be quite different from those in higher eukaryotes.
, although the mRNA-protein concordance is generally high, the discordance is also substantial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mRNA-protein concordance should be explicitly tested and not assumed a priori, as this may lead to erroneous conclusions in systems analyses.
the dynamic nature of biological processes is likely reflected by divergent mRNA-protein trends, and that such trends may be indicative of the underlying regulatory mechanisms.
the dynamic nature of biological processes is not only a function of the time-scale but also a function of the level of analysis.
